text:
Oliver Moore is the fastest thing on a lot of nights in Chicago. His 68 bursts over 20 mph rank in the 95th percentile, and that speed is the reason the 2023 19th overall pick is getting regular minutes at 21. The production hasn't followed yet: three goals and six points in 22 games, 0.27 points a game against a median of 0.36 for forwards drafted around him in their first full season.

There's real bad luck in that gap. The Blackhawks have scored 4.7 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, which has cost him points, and his on-ice expected-goal share is 6.4 points better than the team's without him. Against Toronto he had one goal wiped out by a review and still scored another.

Evolving-Hockey liked his defense last season (opponents got 0.11 fewer expected goals per 60 with him out there) and noted he played with some of the weakest linemates in the league. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking doesn't see a standout strength yet. His ice time is up about a minute lately; if the goals start matching the chances, our range has him around 28 points.
